About this dashboard

Hide

Goal: Provide a unified, real-time view of A320 fuselage assembly performance, ensuring production remains on track in terms of quality, cost, and delivery. The dashboard enables early identification of critical path deviations, elimination of non-value-added activities, and optimization of manufacturing processes through Lean principles, including Kanban, Just-in-Time (JIT), and Just-in-Sequence (JIS).

By integrating AI Agents, Edge AI, Digital Twins, Industrial Metaverse, and Cloud technologies, the solution enables proactive detection and prediction of supply chain, quality, and production disruptions. This supports faster, data-driven decision-making, minimizes downtime, reduces scrap and rework, and improves right-first-time performance, contributing to the production target of 100 aircraft per month.

The dashboard also provides end-to-end visibility into multi-agent orchestration, illustrating how specialized AI agents collaborate, exchange information, coordinate decisions, and execute complex, multi-step workflows as a unified, goal-driven system. This transparency enables stakeholders to monitor agent activities, understand automated decisions, track issue resolution, and maintain human oversight of critical manufacturing operations.

Who it is for

Shift and line leads, quality engineers, production planners and the project team responsible for fuselage assembly.

What the agents do

  • Read SAP QM, SAP MM, MES confirmations, inspection records and torque logs
  • Classify each quality notification and assign an owner
  • Keep the scrap Pareto and section status current
  • Compute right first time per station and shift
  • Open an 8D when a limit is crossed and escalate to the shift lead
  • Draft the shift handover

How to read it

  • Top: the four KPIs against the previous 7 days and their targets
  • Middle: where the problems sit: defect mix, fuselage sections, scrap drivers, stations
  • Join cell twin: the robot agents riveting the section 15/21 join, live in 3D
  • Bottom: agent orchestration, showing how the agents share and hand over the work
  • Right: ask the line assistant for causes, held sections or a handover

What it should achieve

  • Faster reaction to quality and scrap events
  • Fewer repeat defects through early root-cause work
  • Less manual KPI collection and reporting
  • One shared picture of the line across shifts
